text: The percentage error in the calculated volume of a sphere, if there is $2%$ error in its diameter measurement, is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The volume $V$ of a sphere is given by the formula $V=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}$, where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Since the error is given in terms of diameter (D), we express the radius as $r=\frac{D}{2}$.

Substituting this into the volume formula:

$\mathrm{V}=\frac{4}{3}π\left (\frac{\mathrm{D}}{2}\right )^{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{V}=\frac{4}{3}π\left (\frac{\mathrm{D}^{3}}{8}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $V=\frac{1}{6}πD^{3}$

To find the relative error, we take the natural logarithm $(\ln )$ on both sides of the equation :

$\ln (V)=\ln \left (\frac{π}{6}\right )+\ln \left (D^{3}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\ln (V)=\ln \left (\frac{π}{6}\right )+3\ln (D)$

Now, on differentiating both sides.

$\frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{V}}=0+3\left (\frac{\mathrm{dD}}{\mathrm{D}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{V}}=3\frac{\mathrm{dD}}{\mathrm{D}}$

To express this as a percentage error, we multiply both sides by 100 :

$\left (\frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{V}}\times 100\right )=3\times \left (\frac{\mathrm{dD}}{\mathrm{D}}\times 100\right )$

It is given that the percentage error in the diameter is $2%$.

$\frac{dD}{D}\times 100=2%$

So, percentage error in Volume $=3\times 2%$

Percentage error in Volume $=6%$

Therefore, the correct option is (C).

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the dimensional equation of Boltzmann Constant $(k_{B})$

The average kinetic energy (E) of a gas molecule is related to temperature (T) by the equation :

$\mathrm{E}=\frac{3}{2}\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{B}}\mathrm{T}$

To find the dimensions of $\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{B}}$ :

$[\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{B}}]=\frac{[\mathrm{E}]}{[\mathrm{T}]}$

Using the formula Work $=$ Force × Distance, dimensions of energy is $[\mathrm{E}]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]$

The dimensions of temperature is $[\mathrm{T}]=[\mathrm{K}]$

So,

$[\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{B}}]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ][\mathrm{K}]^{-1}=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\right ]$

Thus, (A) Boltzmann constant → (III) [ $\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$ ]

For the dimensions of Stefan's Constant ( $σ$ )

According to Stefan-Boltzmann law, the energy radiated per unit area per unit time $(\mathrm{P})$ is:

$\mathrm{P}=σ\mathrm{T}^{4}$

Where $\mathrm{P}=\frac{\text{Energy}}{\text{Area× Time}}$

Dimensions of

$[\mathrm{P}]=\frac{\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]}{[\mathrm{L}^{2}][\mathrm{T}]}=\left [\mathrm{MT}^{-3}\right ]$

Dimensions of $\mathrm{T}^{4}$ is $\left [\mathrm{K}^{4}\right ]$

So, the dimensions of Stefan's constant is

$[σ]=\frac{[\mathrm{P}]}{[\mathrm{T}^{4}]}=\frac{\left [\mathrm{MT}^{-3}\right ]}{[\mathrm{K}^{4}]}=\left [\mathrm{MT}^{-3}\mathrm{K}^{-4}\right ]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{-3}\mathrm{K}^{-4}\right ]$

Thus, (B) Stefan's constant → (IV)[ $\mathrm{ML}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{-3}\mathrm{K}^{-4}$ ]

For the dimensions of Planck's Constant (h):

The energy (E) of a photon is given by $E=hν$, where $ν$ is frequency (Time ${}^{-1}$ ).

So, the dimension of Planck's constant is

$[\mathrm{h}]=\frac{[\mathrm{E}]}{[v]}=\frac{\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]}{[\mathrm{T}^{-1}]}$

$\Rightarrow$ $[\mathrm{h}]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right ]$

Thus, (C) Planck's constant → (II)[ $\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-1}$ ]

For the dimensions of Gravitational Constant (G):

From Newton's law of gravitation $F=\frac{Gm_{1}m_{2}}{r^{2}}\Rightarrow G=\frac{Fr^{2}}{m_{1}m_{2}}$

The dimensions of Force is $[\mathrm{F}]=\left [\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right ]$

The dimensions of Distance squared is $\left [\mathrm{r}^{2}\right ]=\left [\mathrm{L}^{2}\right ]$

The dimensions of mass squared is $[\mathrm{m}_{1}\mathrm{m}_{2}]=\left [\mathrm{M}^{2}\right ]$

So, the dimensions of Gravitational constant is

$[\mathrm{G}]=\frac{\left [\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right ]\left [\mathrm{L}^{2}\right ]}{[\mathrm{M}^{2}]}=\left [\mathrm{M}^{-1}\mathrm{L}^{3}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]$

Thus (D) Gravitational constant $\to$ (I) $\left [\mathrm{M}^{-1}\mathrm{L}^{3}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]$

$\mathrm{A}\to \mathrm{III},\mathrm{B}\to \mathrm{IV},\mathrm{C}\to \mathrm{II},\mathrm{D}\to \mathrm{I}$

Therefore, the correct option is (C).

text: A solid sphere $(A)$ of mass $5m$ and a spherical shell $(B)$ of mass $m$, both having same radius, are placed on a rough surface. When a force of same magnitude is applied tangentially at the highest points of $A$ and $B$, they start rolling without slipping with an acceleration of $a_{A}$ and $a_{B}$, respectively. The ratio of $a_{A}$ and $a_{B}$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a body of mass $M$, radius $R$ and moment of inertia $I$ pulled by $F$ at its highest point, take the friction $f$ at the contact point along $F$:


[IMG]

Translation: $F+f=Ma$

Rotation about the centre, with $α=\dfrac{a}{R}$ for rolling without slipping: $(F-f)R=I\dfrac{a}{R}\Rightarrow F-f=\dfrac{I}{R^{2}}a$

Adding the two equations eliminates $f$:

$2F=\left (M+\dfrac{I}{R^{2}}\right )a\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{2F}{M+\dfrac{I}{R^{2}}}$

Solid sphere A: $M=5m$ and $\dfrac{I}{R^{2}}=\dfrac{2}{5}(5m)=2m$, so $a_{A}=\dfrac{2F}{7m}$.

Spherical shell B: $M=m$ and $\dfrac{I}{R^{2}}=\dfrac{2}{3}m$, so $a_{B}=\dfrac{2F}{\frac{5}{3}m}=\dfrac{6F}{5m}$.

$\dfrac{a_{A}}{a_{B}}=\dfrac{2F}{7m}\times \dfrac{5m}{6F}=\dfrac{10}{42}=\dfrac{5}{21}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: A body of mass 1 kg moves along a straight line with a velocity $v=2x^{2}$. The work done by the body during displacement from $x=0$ to 5 m is $____$ J.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Work done (W) is defined as the integral of force (F) over a displacement (dx):

$\mathrm{W}=\int\limits _{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}}^{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{f}}}\mathrm{Fdx}$

From Newton's Second Law, $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{ma}$, and acceleration $\mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}$.

Using the chain rule, $\mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dx}}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{v}\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dx}}$.

$W=\int\limits _{x_{i}}^{x_{f}}\left [m\left (v\frac{dv}{dx}\right )\right ]dx$

$\Rightarrow$ $W=\int\limits _{v_{i}}^{v_{f}}mvdv=m\int\limits _{v_{i}}^{v_{f}}vdv=m\left [\frac{v^{2}}{2}\right ]_{v_{i}}^{v_{f}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=\Delta \mathrm{K}.\mathrm{E}.$

The mass of the body is $\mathrm{m}=1\mathrm{kg}$

The velocity of body is given as function of position, $\mathrm{v}=2\mathrm{x}^{2}$

Initial position is $\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}=0\mathrm{m}$

Final position is $\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{f}}=5\mathrm{m}$

At $\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}=0$ :

$\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{i}}=2(0)^{2}=0\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

At $\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{f}}=5$ :

$v_{f}=2(5)^{2}=2(25)=50\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

On substituting these values into the Work-Energy equation :

$\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{m}\left (\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}-\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{2}\times 1\times \left (50^{2}-0^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{2}\times (2500)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=1250\mathrm{J}$

Therefore, the work done by the body during displacement from $\mathrm{x}=0$ to $\mathrm{x}=5\mathrm{m}$ is 1250 J . 

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: A cylinder with adiabatic walls is closed at both ends and is divided into two compartments by a frictionless adiabatic piston. Ideal gas is filled in both (left and right) the compartments at same $P,V,T$. Heating is started from left side until pressure changes to $27\mathrm{P}/8$. If initial volume of each compartment was 9 litres then the final volume in right-hand side compartment is $____$ litres. (for this ideal gas $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}}/\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}=1.5$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In left compartment heat is added. The gas expands, increasing its pressure and volume.

In right compartment heat is not added because the wall is adiabatic, but the piston moves toward it because the pressure on the left increases. Since the walls and the piston are adiabatic, the gas in the right compartment undergoes an adiabatic compression.

The piston stops moving when the pressure in both compartments is equal. Therefore, the final pressure in the right compartment $(\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{R}})$ will also be $\frac{27\mathrm{P}}{8}$.


[IMG]


For an adiabatic process, the relationship between pressure $(\mathrm{P})$ and volume $(\mathrm{V})$ is:

$\mathrm{P}\mathrm{V}^{γ}=\text{constant}$

Where $γ=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}}=1.5$.

$P_{1}V_{1}^{γ}=P_{2}V_{2}^{γ}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}=\left (\frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}\right )^{1/γ}$

The initial pressure in right compartment is $\mathrm{P}_{1}=\mathrm{P}$ and its initial volume is $\mathrm{V}_{1}=9$ litres

The final pressure in right compartment is $\mathrm{P}_{2}=\frac{27\mathrm{P}}{8}$

Substituting these values:

$\frac{V_{\text{final}}}{9}=\left (\frac{P}{27P/8}\right )^{1/1.5}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\text{final}}}{9}=\left (\frac{8}{27}\right )^{2/3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{V_{\text{final}}}{9}=\frac{4}{9}$

$\Rightarrow$ $V_{\text{final}}=4\text{litres}$

Therefore, the final volume in the right-hand side compartment is 4 litres. 

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: For an electromagnetic wave propagating through vacuum, $⃗{k},⃗{E}$ and $ω$ represent propagation vector, electric field and angular frequency, respectively. The magnetic field associated with this wave is represented by:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field $⃗{E}$, magnetic field $⃗{B}$, and the propagation direction $⃗{k}$ are mutually perpendicular to each other. The wave travels in the direction of the cross product $\vec{\mathrm{E}}\times \vec{\mathrm{B}}$.

Also the magnetic field vector is in the direction of $\widehat{\mathrm{k}}\times \widehat{\mathrm{E}}$

The magnitude of magnetic field is given as $\mathrm{B}=\frac{\mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{c}}$, where c is the speed of light.

Maxwell's equation (Faraday's Law) in differential form is :

$\nabla \times \vec{\mathrm{E}}=-\frac{𝜕\vec{\mathrm{B}}}{𝜕\mathrm{t}}$

For a plane monochromatic wave, the fields can be represented asb :

$\vec{\mathrm{E}}=\vec{\mathrm{E}}_{0}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}(\vec{\mathrm{k}}\cdot \vec{\mathrm{r}}-ω\mathrm{t})}$

$\vec{\mathrm{B}}=\vec{\mathrm{B}}_{0}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}(\vec{\mathrm{k}}\cdot \vec{\mathrm{r}}-ω\mathrm{t})}$

Applying the curl operator ( $\nabla \times$ ) to the electric field expression :

$\nabla \times \vec{\mathrm{E}}=\mathrm{i}\vec{\mathrm{k}}\times \vec{\mathrm{E}}$

Applying the time derivative to the magnetic field expression :

$\frac{𝜕\vec{\mathrm{B}}}{𝜕\mathrm{t}}=-\mathrm{i}ω\mathrm{B}\leftarrow$

Substituting into Faraday's Law :

$\mathrm{i}\vec{\mathrm{k}}\times \vec{\mathrm{E}}=-(-\mathrm{i}ω\mathrm{B}\leftarrow )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{i}\vec{\mathrm{k}}\times \vec{\mathrm{E}}=\mathrm{i}ω\vec{\mathrm{B}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{\vec{\mathrm{k}}\times \vec{\mathrm{E}}}{ω}$

Therefore, the correct option is (B)

text: Two identical bodies A and B of equal masses have initial velocities $\vec{v_{1}}=4\hat{i}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and $\vec{v_{2}}=4\hat{j}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ respectively. The body A has acceleration $\vec{a_{1}}=6\hat{i}+6\hat{j}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ while the acceleration of the other body B is zero. The centre of mass of the two bodies moves in $____$ path.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For two bodies of equal mass $(\mathrm{m}_{1}=\mathrm{m}_{2}=\mathrm{m})$, the velocity of the COM is:

$\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{\mathrm{m}\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{1}+\mathrm{m}\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{2}}{\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{1}+\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{2}}{2}$

The velocity of body $A$ is $⃗{v}_{1}=4\hat{i}$ and that of body $B$ it is $⃗{v}_{2}=4\hat{j}$ :

So,

$\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{4\hat{ı}+4\hat{ȷ}}{2}=(2\hat{ı}+2\hat{ȷ})\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Similarly, for equal masses the acceleration of center of mass is,

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{1}+\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{2}}{2}$

The acceleration of body A is $\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{1}=6\hat{i}+6\hat{\mathrm{j}}$ and that of body B is $\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{2}=0$ :

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{(6\hat{ı}+6\hat{ȷ})+0}{2}=(3\hat{ı}+3\hat{ȷ})\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

A particle moves in a straight line if its acceleration vector is parallel (or anti-parallel) to its velocity vector. If they are not parallel, the path is generally a parabola (under constant acceleration).

Direction of velocity of centre of mass is,

$\tan θ_{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}}{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}}=\frac{2}{2}=1\Rightarrow θ_{\mathrm{v}}=\tan ^{-1}(1)=\frac{π}{4}\mathrm{rad}$

Direction of acceleration of centre of mass is,

$\tan θ_{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{y}}}{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{x}}}=\frac{3}{3}=1\Rightarrow θ_{\mathrm{a}}=\tan ^{-1}(1)=\frac{π}{4}\mathrm{rad}$

Since both vectors have the same direction (they both make an angle of $45^{\circ }$ with the positive x -axis), the acceleration is acting exactly along the line of motion.

Because $\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is parallel to $\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{\mathrm{cm}}$, the center of mass moves in a straight line. Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Figure represents the extension $(\Delta l)$ of a wire of length 1 meter, suspended from the ceiling of the room at one end with a load $W$ connected to the other end. If the cross-sectional area of the wire is $10^{-5}\mathrm{m}^{2}$ then the Young's modulus of the wire is $____$ $\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Young's Modulus (Y) is defined as the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain within the elastic limit.

Stress ( $σ$ ) is force (W) per unit cross-sectional area (A).

$σ=\frac{W}{A}$

Strain $(𝜖)$ is extension $(\Delta \mathrm{l})$ per unit original length $(\mathrm{L})$.

$𝜖=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}}{\mathrm{L}}$

Thus, Young's Modulus is :

$Y=\frac{σ}{𝜖}=\frac{W/A}{\Delta l/L}$

$\mathrm{Y}=\frac{\mathrm{WL}}{\mathrm{A}\Delta \mathrm{l}}$

The original length is $\mathrm{L}=1\mathrm{m}$

The cross-sectional area is $\mathrm{A}=10^{-5}\mathrm{m}^{2}$

From the graph, we need a pair of values for W and $\Delta \mathrm{l}$.

Let's take $\mathrm{W}=20\mathrm{N}$ and the corresponding extension $\Delta \mathrm{l}=2\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}$.


[IMG]


Substituting the values in the expression for Young's modulus;

$Y=\frac{20\times 1}{10^{-5}\times \left (2\times 10^{-4}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow$ $Y=\frac{20}{2\times 10^{-9}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $Y=10\times 10^{9}$

$\mathrm{Y}=1.0\times 10^{10}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$

Therefore, the Young's modulus of the wire is $1.0\times 10^{10}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$. Thus, the correct option is (C).

text: A cylindrical vessel of 40 cm radius is completely filled with water and its capacity is $528\mathrm{dm}^{3}$ (dm : decimeter) The vessel is placed on a solid block of exactly same height as vessel. If a small hole is made at 70 cm below the top of water level, then horizontal range of water falling on the ground in the beginning is $____$ cm .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The capacity of vessel is $528\mathrm{dm}^{3}$.

Since $1\mathrm{dm}=10\mathrm{cm}\Rightarrow 1\mathrm{dm}^{3}=1000\mathrm{cm}^{3}$

$\mathrm{V}=528,000\mathrm{cm}^{3}$

Volume of a cylinder is $\mathrm{V}=π\mathrm{r}^{2}\mathrm{H}$.

Given $\mathrm{r}=40\mathrm{cm}$

$528,000=\times H$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{528,000}{π\times (40)^{2}}=\mathrm{H}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{H}=105\mathrm{cm}$

Depth of hole from top is $\mathrm{h}=70\mathrm{cm}$.


[IMG]


From Torricelli's Law velocity of efflux is given as,

$\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{2\mathrm{gh}}$

The vessel is on a block of height H and the hole is at distance $(\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{h})$ from the bottom of the vessel.

Total height from ground $\mathrm{Y}=(\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{h})+\mathrm{H}=2\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{h}$

The time to fall is,

$t=\sqrt{\frac{2Y}{g}}$

The horizontal range of projectile is given as

$\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{v}\times \mathrm{t}=\sqrt{2\mathrm{gh}}\times \sqrt{\frac{2(2\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{h})}{\mathrm{g}}}=2\sqrt{\mathrm{h}(2\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{h})}$

The height of water level from the hole is $\mathrm{h}=70\mathrm{cm}$

$2\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{h}=2(105)-70=210-70=140\mathrm{cm}.$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{R}=2\sqrt{70\times 140}$

$\Rightarrow$ $R=2\sqrt{70\times 70\times 2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{R}=2\times 70\times \sqrt{2}=140\sqrt{2}\mathrm{cm}$

Therefore, the horizontal of water falling on the ground is $140\sqrt{2}\mathrm{cm}$. 

Thus. the correct option is (B).

text: If 2 mole of an ideal monoatomic gas at temperature $T$, is mixed with 6 mole of another ideal monoatomic gas at temperature $2T$ then the temperature of mixture is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The internal energy $(U)$ of $n$ moles of an ideal gas at temperature $T$ is given by $U=nC_{v}T$, where $C_{v}$ is the molar specific heat at constant volume.

For the mixture, total initial internal energy $\mathrm{U}_{\text{initial}}=\mathrm{U}_{1}+\mathrm{U}_{2}$

Total final internal energy $\mathrm{U}_{\text{final}}=(\mathrm{n}_{1}+\mathrm{n}_{2})\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v},\text{mix}}\mathrm{T}_{\text{mix}}$

Since both gases are monoatomic, their molar specific heats are the same,

$C_{v1}=C_{v2}=C_{v,\mathrm{mix}}=\frac{3}{2}R$

Therefore, using conservation of energy (total initial internal energy is equal to final internal energy).

$\mathrm{n}_{1}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}\mathrm{T}_{1}+\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}\mathrm{T}_{2}=(\mathrm{n}_{1}+\mathrm{n}_{2})\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{mix}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{mix}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_{1}\mathrm{T}_{1}+\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{T}_{2}}{(\mathrm{n}_{1}+\mathrm{n}_{2})}$

Moles of first gas is $\mathrm{n}_{1}=2$

Temperature of first gas is $\mathrm{T}_{1}=\mathrm{T}$

Moles of second gas $\mathrm{n}_{2}=6$

Temperature of second gas $\mathrm{T}_{2}=2\mathrm{T}$

On substituting the values into expression for the temperature of mixture,

$\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{mix}}=\frac{(2\times \mathrm{T})+(6\times 2\mathrm{T})}{2+6}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{mix}}=\frac{2\mathrm{T}+12\mathrm{T}}{8}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{mix}}=\frac{14\mathrm{T}}{8}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{mix}}=\frac{7}{4}\mathrm{T}$

Therefore, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
A spring stretches by 2 mm when it is loaded with a mass of 200 g . From equilibrium position the mass is further pulled down by 2 mm and released. The frequency associated with the system and maximum energy in the spring are $____$ Hz and $____$ J, respectively.

(Take $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]
When the mass is at rest (equilibrium), the downward gravitational force is balanced by the upward spring force.

$\mathrm{mg}=\mathrm{kx}_{0}$

Where, mass of the suspended load is $\mathrm{m}=200\mathrm{g}=0.2\mathrm{kg}$,

The acceleration due to gravity is $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$,

The extension in spring at equilibrium position is $x_{0}=2\mathrm{mm}=2\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{m}$

Putting the values,

$\mathrm{k}=\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{x}_{0}}=\frac{0.2\times 10}{2\times 10^{-3}}=\frac{2}{2}\times 10^{3}=1000\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$

The angular frequency ( $ω$ ) of a mass-spring system is derived from the restoration force $\mathrm{F}=-\mathrm{kx}$.

Since $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{ma}$, we have $\mathrm{ma}+\mathrm{kx}=0$,

$ω=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}}$

The linear frequency is $f=\frac{ω}{2π}$ :

$\mathrm{f}=\frac{1}{2π}\sqrt{\frac{1000}{0.2}}=\frac{1}{2π}\sqrt{5000}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{f}=\frac{1}{2π}\sqrt{100\times 50}=\frac{10\sqrt{50}}{2π}=\frac{5\sqrt{50}}{π}\mathrm{Hz}$

The mass is pulled down a further 2 mm from equilibrium and released. This additional displacement is the amplitude (A).

$A=2\mathrm{mm}=2\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{m}$

The maximum energy in the spring is at the point of maximum extension, i.e., $x_{\max }=4\mathrm{mm}=4\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{m}$

$\mathrm{E}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{kx}_{\max }^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E=\frac{1}{2}\times 1000\times \left (4\times 10^{-3}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{E}=500\times \left (16\times 10^{-6}\right )=8000\times 10^{-6}=8\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{J}$

Therefore, the frequency associated with the system is $\frac{5\sqrt{50}}{π}\mathrm{Hz}$ and the maximum energy in the spring is $8\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{J}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (A).

text: The electric potential as a function of $x,y$ is given by $V=5\left (x^{2}-y^{2}\right )V$. The electric field at a point $(2,3)\mathrm{m}$ is $____$ $\mathrm{V}/\mathrm{m}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The electric field is the negative gradient of the potential:

$⃗{E}=-\nabla V=-\left (\dfrac{𝜕V}{𝜕x}\hat{i}+\dfrac{𝜕V}{𝜕y}\hat{j}\right )$

With $V=5x^{2}-5y^{2}$:

$E_{x}=-\dfrac{𝜕V}{𝜕x}=-10x,E_{y}=-\dfrac{𝜕V}{𝜕y}=-(-10y)=10y$

At $(2,3)\text{m}$: $E_{x}=-10(2)=-20\text{V m}^{-1}$ and $E_{y}=10(3)=30\text{V m}^{-1}$.

$⃗{E}=(-20\hat{i}+30\hat{j})\text{V m}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
A current of 30 A each flows in opposite directions in two conducting wires, placed parallel to each other at a distance of 8 cm . The magnetic field at the mid point between the two wires is $____$ $μ\mathrm{T}$.

$\left (\frac{μ_{\mathrm{o}}}{4π}=10^{-7}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{A}^{2}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to the Ampere's circuital Law, the magnetic field B at a distance r from an infinitely long straight wire carrying current I is :

$\int \vec{\mathrm{B}}\cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{\mathrm{l}}=μ_{0}\mathrm{I}$

For a circular path of radius $r$ :

$B(2πr)=μ_{0}I\Rightarrow B=\frac{μ_{0}I}{2πr}$

Let the wires be $\mathrm{W}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{W}_{2}$ separated by $\mathrm{d}=8\mathrm{cm}$. The midpoint is at $\mathrm{r}=4\mathrm{cm}=0.04\mathrm{m}$ from each wire.

Wire 1 carries current along out of the page. Using the right-hand rule, the field $\mathrm{B}_{1}$ at the midpoint points along $y$-axis.

Wire 2 carries current along into the page. Using the right-hand rule, the field $\mathrm{B}_{2}$ at the midpoint also points along y -axis.


[IMG]


Since both fields point in the same direction, the net magnetic field $\mathrm{B}_{\text{net}}=\mathrm{B}_{1}+\mathrm{B}_{2}$.

The current in the wires are given as $\mathrm{I}_{1}=\mathrm{I}_{2}=30\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{r}=0.04\mathrm{m}$ :

$B_{1}=B_{2}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{2πr}=2\times \left (\frac{μ_{0}}{4π}\right )\frac{I}{r}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{B}_{1}=\mathrm{B}_{2}=2\times 10^{-7}\times \frac{30}{0.04}=2\times 10^{-7}\times 750=15\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{T}$

$\Rightarrow$ $B_{\text{net}}=15\times 10^{-5}+15\times 10^{-5}=30\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{T}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{net}}=300\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{T}=300μ\mathrm{T}$

Therefore, the magnitude of magnetic field at the midpoint is $300μ\mathrm{T}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text: A square loop of side 2 cm is placed in a time varying magnetic field with magnitude as $B=0.4\sin (300t)$ Tesla. The normal to the plane of loop makes an angle of $60^{\circ }$ with the field. The maximum induced emf produced in the loop is $____$ mV .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Magnetic flux $𝜙$ through a loop is $𝜙=\vec{\mathrm{B}}\cdot \vec{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{BA}\cos θ$.

According to Faraday's Law, the induced emf $ε$ is the negative rate of change of flux:

$ε=-\frac{\mathrm{d}𝜙}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dt}}(\mathrm{BA}\cos θ)$

Since area (A) and angle ( $θ$ ) are constant.

$ε=-\mathrm{A}\cos θ\frac{\mathrm{dB}}{\mathrm{dt}}$

The length of side of square is $\mathrm{s}=2\mathrm{cm}=0.02\mathrm{m}$.

Then the area of loop is,

$A=s^{2}=(0.02)^{2}=4\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}^{2}$

The angle made by magnetic field with the normal to the plane of loop is $θ=60^{\circ }$

The time varying magnetic field is $B=0.4\sin (300t)$.

The rate of change of magnetic field is

$\frac{\mathrm{dB}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dt}}(0.4\sin (300\mathrm{t}))=0.4\times 300\cos (300\mathrm{t})=120\cos (300\mathrm{t})$

Substituting into the emf equation :

$ε=-\left (4\times 10^{-4}\right )\cos (60^{\circ })[120\cos (300\mathrm{t})]$

$\Rightarrow$ $ε=-\left (4\times 10^{-4}\right )\times 0.5\times 120\cos (300t)=-0.024\cos (300t)V$

The maximum induced emf $\left (ε_{\text{\max }}\right )$ occurs when $\cos (300t)=1$ :

$ε_{\max }=0.024\mathrm{V}=24\mathrm{mV}$

Therefore, the magnitude of maximum induced emf is 24 mV . 

Thus, the correct option is (D).

text:
A sphere of capacitance 100 pF is charged to a potential of 100 V . Another identical uncharged metal sphere is brought in contact with the charged sphere, then the change in the total energy stored on these spheres, when they touch is $α\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{J}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .

(combined capacitance of spheres is 200 pF )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The work done in charging a capacitor is stored as electrostatic potential energy. If a charge dq is moved to a capacitor of capacitance C at potential $\mathrm{V}=\mathrm{q}/\mathrm{C}$, the work dW is:

$\mathrm{dW}=\mathrm{Vdq}=\frac{\mathrm{q}}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{dq}$

Integrating from $\mathrm{q}=0$ to total charge $\mathrm{q}=\mathrm{Q}$ :

$\mathrm{U}=\int\limits _{0}^{\mathrm{Q}}\frac{\mathrm{q}}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{dq}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{c}}\int\limits _{0}^{\mathrm{Q}}\mathrm{qdq}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}^{2}}{2\mathrm{C}}$

Using $\mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{CV}$,

$\mathrm{U}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{CV}^{2}$

Initially, only the first sphere ( $\mathrm{C}_{1}=100\mathrm{pF}$ ) is charged to $\mathrm{V}_{1}=100\mathrm{V}$.

$U_{i}=\frac{1}{2}C_{1}V_{1}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $U_{i}=\frac{1}{2}\times \left (100\times 10^{-12}\right )\times (100)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=\frac{1}{2}\times 10^{-10}\times 10^{4}=0.5\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{J}=5\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{J}$

Finally, when the spheres touch, they share charge until they reach a common potential $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{c}}$.

Since the spheres are identical ( $\mathrm{C}_{1}=\mathrm{C}_{2}=100\mathrm{pF}$ ), the charge Q is shared equally, and

$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{\text{Total Charge}}{\text{Total Capacitance}}=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{1}\mathrm{V}_{1}+0}{\mathrm{C}_{1}+\mathrm{C}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}_{1}}{2}=50\mathrm{V}.$

So, the final energy is,

$U_{f}=\frac{1}{2}(C_{1}+C_{2})V_{c}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $U_{f}=\frac{1}{2}\times \left (200\times 10^{-12}\right )\times (50)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $U_{f}=100\times 10^{-12}\times 2500=2.5\times 10^{-7}J$

So, the change in energy is,

$\Delta U=U_{i}-U_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{U}=5\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{J}-2.5\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{J}=2.5\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{J}=α\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{J}$

$\Rightarrow α=2.5=\frac{5}{2}$

text:
The energy released if hydrogen atoms are combined to form ${}_{2}^{4}\mathrm{He}$ is $____$ MeV .

(Take binding energies per nucleon of ${}_{1}^{2}\mathrm{H}$ and ${}_{2}^{4}\mathrm{He}$ as 1.1 MeV and 7.2 MeV , respectively)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The binding energy (B.E.) of a nucleus is the energy required to disassemble it into its constituent nucleons.

Total B.E. $=($ Binding Energy per nucleon $)\times ($ Number of nucleons A$)$

Energy Released (Q) = (Total B.E. of Products) - (Total B.E. of Reactants)

The given reaction is $\mathrm{H}_{1}^{2}+\mathrm{H}_{1}^{2}\to \mathrm{He}_{2}^{4}$

The reactants are two nuclei of $\mathrm{H}_{1}^{2}$.

B.E. per nucleon of $\mathrm{H}_{1}^{2}=1.1\mathrm{MeV}$

Number of nucleons (A) for one $\mathrm{H}_{1}^{2}=2$

So, total B.E. of reactants $=2\times (1.1\times 2)=4.4\mathrm{MeV}$

The product is one nucleus of $\mathrm{He}_{2}^{4}$.

B.E. per nucleon of $\mathrm{He}_{2}^{4}=7.2\mathrm{MeV}$

Number of nucleons (A) for $\mathrm{He}_{2}^{4}=4$

So, total B.E. of product $=7.2\times 4=28.8\mathrm{MeV}$

Hence, energy released during reaction is,

$\mathrm{Q}=28.8\mathrm{MeV}-4.4\mathrm{MeV}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{Q}=24.4\mathrm{MeV}$

Therefore, the energy released if hydrogen atoms are combined to form $\mathrm{He}_{2}^{4}$ is 24.4 MeV . 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text: Angle of minimum deviation is equal to the half of the angle of prism in an equilateral prism. The refractive index of the prism is $____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a prism with angle A and refractive index $μ$, the relationship between the angle of minimum deviation ( $δ_{\mathrm{m}}$ ) and refractive index is given by:

$μ=\frac{\sin \left (\frac{A+δm}{2}\right )}{\sin \left (\frac{A}{2}\right )}$

For equilateral prism the angle of the prism is $\mathrm{A}=60^{\circ }$.

The angle of minimum deviation is half the angle of prism $\left (δ_{m}=\frac{A}{2}\right )$.

Therefore, $δ_{m}=\frac{60^{\circ }}{2}=30^{\circ }$

Substituting $\mathrm{A}=60^{\circ }$ and $δ_{\mathrm{m}}=30^{\circ }$ into the formula:

$μ=\frac{\sin \left (\frac{60\circ +30\circ }{2}\right )}{\sin \left (\frac{60\circ }{2}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow$ $μ=\frac{\sin (45^{\circ })}{\sin (30^{\circ })}$

$\Rightarrow$ $μ=\frac{1/\sqrt{2}}{1/2}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $μ=\sqrt{2}$

Therefore, the refractive index of the prism is $\sqrt{2}$. 

Thus the correct option is (C).

text:
The velocity at which 6 kg mass (shown in figure) strikes the ground when it is released from a height of 6 m above the ground is $____$ $\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. Assume pulley is massless and string is light and inextensible. (Take $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ )

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the 6 kg mass $(\mathrm{M})$ moving down and the 2 kg mass $(\mathrm{m})$ moving up, let the acceleration of system is a and tension in the string is T .


[IMG]


Using Newton's second law ( $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{ma}$ ) of motion for M

$\mathrm{Mg}-\mathrm{T}=\mathrm{Ma}\ldots (i)$

For m ,

$\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{mg}=\mathrm{ma}\ldots (ii)$

Adding the two equations :

$(M-m)g=(M+m)a$

$\Rightarrow$ $a=\frac{(M-m)}{M+m}g$

Substituting $\mathrm{M}=6,\mathrm{m}=2$, and $\mathrm{g}=10$ :

$\mathrm{a}=\frac{6-2}{6+2}\times 10=\frac{4}{8}\times 10=5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

Using the kinematic equation for constant acceleration, starting from rest ( $u=0$ ) :

 $\mathrm{v}^{2}=\mathrm{u}^{2}+2\mathrm{as}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{2\mathrm{as}}$

Where s is the height $\mathrm{h}=6\mathrm{m}$.

$v=\sqrt{2\times 5\times 6}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{60}\approx 7.745\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Therefore, the velocity is approximately $7.74\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. 

The correct option is (A).

text:
In a Young double slit experiment, the wavelength of incident light is $6000\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{o}}$, the separation between slits $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ is 5 cm and the distance between slits plane and screen is 50 cm , as shown in the figure below. If the resultant intensity at $P$ is equal to the intensity due to individual slits, the path difference between interfering waves is $____$ Å.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When two waves of intensities $I_{1}$ and $I_{2}$ interfere with a phase difference $𝜙$, the resultant intensity $I_{R}$ is given by:

$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{R}}=\mathrm{I}_{1}+\mathrm{I}_{2}+2\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}\mathrm{I}_{2}}\cos 𝜙$

Since the slits are identical, the intensities due to individual slits are equal ( $\mathrm{I}_{1}=\mathrm{I}_{2}=\mathrm{I}_{0}$ ). The formula simplifies to:

$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{R}}=\mathrm{I}_{0}+\mathrm{I}_{0}+2\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{0}^{2}}\cos 𝜙$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{R}}=2\mathrm{I}_{0}(1+\cos 𝜙)$

Using the trigonometric identity $1+\cos 𝜙=2\cos ^{2}\left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )$

$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{R}}=4\mathrm{I}_{0}\cos ^{2}\left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )$

It is given that the resultant intensity at point P is equal to the intensity of an individual slit:

$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{R}}=\mathrm{I}_{0}$

Substituting this into equation:

$\mathrm{I}_{0}=4\mathrm{I}_{0}\cos ^{2}\left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\cos ^{2}\left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )=\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\cos \left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )=\pm \frac{1}{2}$

For $\cos \left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow \frac{𝜙}{2}=\frac{π}{3}\Rightarrow 𝜙=\frac{2π}{3}$

For $\cos \left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )=-\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow \frac{𝜙}{2}=π-\frac{π}{3}\Rightarrow \frac{𝜙}{2}=\frac{2π}{3}\Rightarrow 𝜙=\frac{4π}{3}$

As we take phase difference in the range $0\leq 𝜙\leq π$, therefore the required phase difference between interfering waves will be $𝜙=\frac{2π}{3}$.

For other values of $𝜙$ which satisfy the condition $\cos ^{2}\left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )=\frac{1}{4}$, the path difference will be same. So, we take the principle solution in the range $0\leq 𝜙\leq π$.

The phase difference is related to the path difference by the formula:

$𝜙=\frac{2π}{λ}(\Delta x)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{x}=\frac{𝜙\cdot λ}{2π}$

The wavelength of light is given as $λ=6000\text{Å}$ and $𝜙=\frac{2π}{3}$ :

$\Delta \mathrm{x}=\frac{\left (\frac{2π}{3}\right )\cdot 6000\text{Å}}{2π}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{x}=\frac{6000}{3}\text{Å}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{x}=2000\text{Å}$

Therefore, the path difference between interfering waves is $2000\text{Å}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (C).

text: A block takes $t$ time to slide down a plane inclined at $45^{\circ }$ to the horizontal. If the surface is made smooth (frictionless), the block takes time $\frac{t}{2}$ to slide down the plane. The coefficient of friction between the block and the inclined plane is $\left (\frac{α}{100}\right )$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a block of mass $m$ is placed on a plane inclined at an angle $θ$ :


[IMG]


Case 1: Rough Surface

The forces acting along the plane are the component of gravity ( $\mathrm{mg}\sin θ$ ) acting downwards and the kinetic friction ( $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{k}}=μ\mathrm{N}=μ\mathrm{mg}\cos θ$ ) acting upwards.

The net force acting along the inclined surface is $\mathrm{F}_{\text{net}}=\mathrm{mg}\sin θ-μ\mathrm{mg}\cos θ$

Using Newton's second law of motion $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{ma}$, the acceleration of block on rough surface is,

$\mathrm{a}_{\text{rough}}=\mathrm{g}(\sin θ-μ\cos θ)$

Case 2: Smooth Surface

Friction is zero ( $μ=0$ ).

The net force acting along the inclined surface is $\mathrm{F}_{\text{net}}=\mathrm{mg}\sin θ$

So, the acceleration of block on smooth surface is,

$\mathrm{a}_{\text{smooth}}=\frac{\mathrm{mg}\sin θ}{\mathrm{m}}=\mathrm{g}\sin θ$

The block starts from rest ( $\mathrm{u}=0$ ) and slides a distance s .

Using the kinematic equation $\mathrm{s}=\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{at}^{2}:$

$s=\frac{1}{2}at^{2}\Rightarrow t=\sqrt{\frac{2s}{a}}$

For a constant distance s , the relationship is $\mathrm{t}\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{a}}}$, or a $\propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{t}^{2}}$.

The angle of inclination is $θ=45^{\circ }$.

The time taken on rough surface is $\mathrm{t}_{\text{rough}}=\mathrm{t}$.

The time taken on smooth surface is $t_{\text{smooth}}=\frac{t}{2}$.

So, the ratio of accelerations is;

$\frac{\mathrm{a}_{\text{smooth}}}{\mathrm{a}_{\text{rough}}}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{t}_{\text{rough}}}{\mathrm{t}_{\text{smooth}}}\right )^{2}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{t}/2}\right )^{2}=(2)^{2}=4$

Substituting the acceleration formulas into the ratio :

$\frac{\mathrm{g}\sin 45^{\circ }}{\mathrm{g}(\sin 45^{\circ }-μ\cos 45^{\circ })}=4$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1/\sqrt{2}}{\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-μ\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )\right )}=4$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{1-μ}=4$

$\Rightarrow$ $1=4-4μ$

$\Rightarrow$ $4μ=3\Rightarrow μ=0.75=\frac{75}{100}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{75}{100}=\frac{α}{100}\Rightarrow α=75$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 75 .

text: The de Broglie wavelength for an electron accelerated through the potential difference of $V_{1}$ volt is $λ_{1}$. When the potential difference is changed to $V_{2}$ volt, the associated de Broglie wavelength is increased by $50%$. If $(V_{1}/V_{2})=(9/α)$, then the value of $α$ is $____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The de Broglie wavelength $λ$ is given by:

$λ=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{p}}$

Where h is Planck's constant and p is the momentum.

The kinetic energy ( $K$ ) of an electron accelerated through a potential $V$ is $K=eV=\frac{p^{2}}{2m}$

$\mathrm{p}=\sqrt{2\mathrm{meV}}$

Substituting p into the wavelength formula:

$λ=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2\mathrm{meV}}}$

For a given particle (electron), the wavelength is inversely proportional to the square root of the potential,

$λ\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$

So, the ratio of wavelengths in two cases is,

$\frac{λ_{2}}{λ_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}}$

The initial wavelength is $λ_{1}$.

The final wavelength is $λ_{2}=λ_{1}+50%$ of $λ_{1}=1.5λ_{1}=\frac{3}{2}λ_{1}$.

Substituting these into the ratio :

$\frac{\frac{3}{2}λ_{1}}{λ_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{3}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\frac{3}{2}\right )^{2}=\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{V}_{1}}{\mathrm{V}_{2}}=\frac{9}{4}=\frac{9}{α}\Rightarrow α=4$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 4 .

text: A moving coil of galvanometer when shunted with $2\Omega$ resistance gives a full scale deflection for a current of 500 mA . When a resistance of $470\Omega$ is connected in series it gives a full scale deflection for 10 V potential applied on it. The value of resistance of galvanometer coil is $____$ $\Omega$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a galvanometer of resistance $G$ is shunted with resistance $S$, the total current I splits. The current through the galvanometer is $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}}$.


[IMG]


The potential across the galvanometer and shunt is equal:

$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}}\mathrm{G}=(\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}})\mathrm{S}$

The resistance of shunt is $\mathrm{S}=2\Omega$ and the current to measure with full deflection is $\mathrm{I}=500\mathrm{mA}=0.5\mathrm{A}$

$I_{g}G=(0.5-I_{g})\times 2$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}}\mathrm{G}=1-2\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}}$

$I_{g}(G+2)=1\Rightarrow I_{g}=\frac{1}{G+2}\ldots (i)$

When a resistance R is connected in series, the total potential V is :


[IMG]


$V=I_{g}(G+R)$

The resistance added in series is given as $\mathrm{R}=470\Omega$ and $\mathrm{V}=10\mathrm{V}$ :

$10=I_{g}(G+470)\Rightarrow I_{g}=\frac{10}{G+470}\ldots (ii)$

Since the full-scale deflection current $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}}$ is constant for the galvanometer,

$\frac{1}{G+2}=\frac{10}{G+470}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{G}+470=10(\mathrm{G}+2)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{G}+470=10\mathrm{G}+20$

$\Rightarrow$ $470-20=10\mathrm{G}-\mathrm{G}$

$\Rightarrow$ $450=9\mathrm{G}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{G}=\frac{450}{9}=50\Omega$

Therefore, the value of resistance of the galvanometer coil is $50\Omega$.

text: Two cells of emfs 1 V and 2 V and internal resistance $2\Omega$ and $1\Omega$, respectively connected in parallel, gave a current of 1 A through an external resistance. If the polarity of one cell is reversed, then value of current through the external resistance will be $\frac{α}{5}\mathrm{A}$. The value of $α$ is $____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When two cells with emfs $ε_{1},ε_{2}$ and internal resistances $r_{1},r_{2}$ are connected in parallel, the equivalent $\mathrm{emf}(ε_{\mathrm{eq}})$ and equivalent internal resistance $(\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{eq}})$ are :

$ε_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{\frac{ε1}{\mathrm{r}1}+\frac{ε2}{\mathrm{r}2}}{\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}2}}=\frac{ε_{1}\mathrm{r}_{2}+ε_{2}\mathrm{r}_{1}}{\mathrm{r}_{1}+\mathrm{r}_{2}}$

$\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_{1}\mathrm{r}_{2}}{\mathrm{r}_{1}+\mathrm{r}_{2}}$

Case 1 : Cells are connected with same polarity


[IMG]


The voltages and internal resistances of two cells are $ε_{1}=1\mathrm{V},\mathrm{r}_{1}=2\Omega$ and $ε_{2}=2\mathrm{V},\mathrm{r}_{2}=1\Omega$.

$ε_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{(1\times 1)+(2\times 2)}{2+1}=\frac{1+4}{3}=\frac{5}{3}\mathrm{V}$

The equivalent internal resistance is,

$\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{2\times 1}{2+1}=\frac{2}{3}\Omega$

The current I through external resistance R is :

$I=\frac{ε_{\mathrm{eq}}}{R+r_{\mathrm{eq}}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $1=\frac{5/3}{\mathrm{R}+\frac{2}{3}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}+\frac{2}{3}=\frac{5}{3}\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}=1\Omega$

Case 2 : Polarity of One Cell Reversed


[IMG]


If we reverse the 1 V cell, its emf becomes -1 V .

The equivalent emf of combination is,

$ε_{\mathrm{eq}}^{'}=\frac{(-1\times 1)+(2\times 2)}{2+1}=\frac{-1+4}{3}=\frac{3}{3}=1\mathrm{V}$

The equivalent internal resistance $\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ remains $\frac{2}{3}\Omega$.

So, the new current $\mathrm{I}^{'}$ across the external resistance is:

$I^{'}=\frac{ε_{\mathrm{eq}}^{'}}{R+r_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\frac{1}{1+\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{1}{5/3}=\frac{3}{5}\mathrm{A}$

It is given that $\mathrm{I}^{'}=\frac{α}{5}$ :

$\frac{3}{5}=\frac{α}{5}\Rightarrow α=3$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 3 .

text:
A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm forms an image which is double the size of object when the object is placed at two different positions. The distance between the two positions of the object is

$____$ cm.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a mirror, magnification is given as $\mathrm{m}=-\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}$, where v is the image distance and u is the object distance.

From the mirror formula $\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$ :

$\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{u-f}{uf}\Rightarrow v=\frac{uf}{u-f}$

Substituting v into the magnification formula:

$\mathrm{m}=-\frac{\mathrm{f}}{\mathrm{u}-\mathrm{f}}=\frac{\mathrm{f}}{\mathrm{f}-\mathrm{u}}$

A concave mirror ( $\mathrm{f}=-10\mathrm{cm}$ ) produces a magnification $|\mathrm{m}|=2$ in two cases:

Case 1 : Real Image ( $\mathrm{m}=-2$ )

$-2=-\frac{10}{-10-\mathrm{u}_{1}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $20+2\mathrm{u}_{1}=-10\Rightarrow 2\mathrm{u}_{1}=-30\Rightarrow \mathrm{u}_{1}=-15\mathrm{cm}$

Case 2 : Virtual Image ( $\mathrm{m}=+2$ )

$2=-\frac{10}{-10-\mathrm{u}_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $-20-2\mathrm{u}_{2}=-10\Rightarrow -2\mathrm{u}_{2}=10\Rightarrow \mathrm{u}_{2}=-5\mathrm{cm}$

The distance between the two object positions is:

$\Delta \mathrm{u}=|\mathrm{u}_{1}-\mathrm{u}_{2}|=|-15-(-5)|=|-10|=10\mathrm{cm}$

Therefore, the distance between the two positions is 10 cm .
